strongest.area: Broad market risk appetite, led by Tesla, Alphabet, and the S&P 500/Nasdaq
strongest.reason: major indices closed higher with the VIX down sharply, and Tesla led megacap gainers, as sentiment improved heading into Nvidia's high-stakes August 26 earnings report

strongest.area: Select cybersecurity names, led by Zscaler
strongest.reason: Zscaler rallied on fresh price-target increases from KeyBanc and Mizuho ahead of earnings season, a rare clearly bullish analyst signal in an otherwise mixed software tape

weakest.area: AI-exposed enterprise software, led by Adobe and Salesforce
weakest.reason: Morgan Stanley downgraded both names again this week (cutting Adobe's price target to $240 from $365) as part of a broader wave of Wall Street caution about AI's disruptive threat to the sector; both stocks are down roughly 31% year-to-date
the Clarity Act's Senate vote was pushed from an imminent decision to a September procedural vote, tempering the week's sharp Bitcoin and Ethereum rally even though prices remain elevated

outlook.nextStep: Nvidia's August 26 earnings report is probably the single biggest catalyst to watch closely across the chip and AI-infrastructure tiers this week. The software-sector downgrades and the Clarity Act delay are probably better treated as ongoing headwinds to monitor than as one-off events to react to.

signals.title: Fed holds steady with a hawkish split; Jackson Hole speech looms
signals.body: July's FOMC meeting minutes, released this week, showed a 9-3 vote to hold rates at 3.50%-3.75%, with three regional Fed presidents dissenting in favor of a hike — an unusually hawkish split. A weaker July jobs report and cooler-than-feared inflation data have pulled September rate-cut odds down somewhat, though the outcome remains genuinely uncertain. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole speech on August 28.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at how Warsh frames the rate path in his Jackson Hole speech, given the hawkish dissent already on record

signals.title: Nvidia's August 26 earnings loom as the week's biggest catalyst
signals.body: Nvidia reports Q2 results after the bell on August 26, with analysts projecting roughly $93-95B in revenue (about 96% year-over-year growth) and price targets clustering between $275 and $325. Chip stocks broadly have struggled to hold gains since July's steep declines on fears about AI-investment returns, though strong cloud growth at Microsoft, Amazon, and Google has helped ease some of that concern.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether Nvidia's results confirm the AI-infrastructure demand story or reignite the ROI-fear narrative from July

signals.title: Morgan Stanley deepens AI-disruption downgrades on Adobe and Salesforce
signals.body: Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Wood downgraded Adobe to Underweight, cutting its price target to $240 from $365, and downgraded Salesforce as well, citing intensifying AI-driven competitive pressure. It's part of a broader wave — more than a dozen firms have downgraded Adobe in 2026 — and both stocks are down roughly 31% year-to-date as the sector reprices AI disruption risk.
signals.focus: lower conviction on the group right now given the persistent and broadening analyst caution

signals.title: Clarity Act vote pushed to September, tempering the week's crypto rally
signals.body: After Bitcoin and Ethereum surged as Trump and crypto executives pushed for a final 2026 vote, the Senate's procedural vote on the Clarity Act has reportedly been pushed to September, with the bill previously viewed by some investors as effectively dead for the year before this latest push. The legislation would clarify whether digital assets are regulated as securities or commodities and is seen as a potential catalyst to end the recent crypto winter.
signals.focus: worth watching whether the September procedural vote actually happens, versus treating this week's price move as a durable regulatory-clarity repricing

signals.title: Zscaler gets fresh price-target hikes ahead of earnings season
signals.body: KeyBanc and Mizuho both raised their price targets on Zscaler to $210 from $185 this week, and the stock rallied on the news. CrowdStrike, meanwhile, heads into its own August 26 earnings report still digesting its summer four-for-one stock split, with Cantor Fitzgerald recently trimming its post-split price target to $250.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether upcoming earnings from CrowdStrike confirm the bullish analyst tone building around Zscaler

signals.title: China's humanoid-robotics space stays a speculative capital magnet
signals.body: UBTECH continues to see volatile trading as speculative capital in China's humanoid-robotics sector rotates between listings following Unitree's blockbuster Shanghai debut. Longer-term forecasts remain bullish — industry estimates put the humanoid-robot market growing from roughly $2-3B today to as much as $200B by 2035 — but near-term single-name moves look more speculative than fundamentals-driven.
signals.focus: worth treating single-day swings in individual robotics names as noise relative to the multi-year capital-flow trend into the space
